title: Connor Love | Andreessen Horowitz
gist: a16z announces Connor Love, a West Point-trained former Army Captain, as a new General Partner in its American Dynamism practice, framing defense/space/manufacturing/autonomous-systems investing as a decade-defining thesis where national-interest alignment and outsized returns reinforce rather than trade off against each other.

insights.claim: a16z's American Dynamism practice is built on the belief that backing companies serving the national interest and generating extraordinary venture returns are not in tension but reinforce each other.
insights.speaker: David Ulevitch
insights.so_what: Signals a16z will keep deploying capital into defense/space/manufacturing on the explicit bet that mission-aligned startups outperform, not just break even on returns versus mission — useful lens for evaluating why the fund keeps doubling down on this category despite it being historically capital-intensive and slow.
insights.quote: serving the country and generating extraordinary returns are not in tension. They reinforce each other.
insights.locator: What convinced us wasn't the track record

insights.claim: a16z believes the next decade will be determined by whether America can build fast enough to stay ahead in defense, space, manufacturing, and autonomous systems, with autonomous systems increasingly serving as the connective layer across the other three.
insights.speaker: David Ulevitch
insights.so_what: Frames autonomous systems as the cross-cutting thesis linking defense, space, and manufacturing bets — worth watching which portfolio companies straddle multiple of these categories as the highest-conviction picks.
insights.quote: The next decade will be defined by whether America can build fast enough to stay ahead, in defense, in space, in manufacturing, and in the autonomous systems that increasingly tie them all together.
insights.locator: The stakes here are only getting higher

insights.claim: a16z considers American Dynamism still early-stage as a category, with many of the companies that will matter most being founded now in areas the broader market has been slow to take seriously.
insights.speaker: David Ulevitch
insights.so_what: A contrarian-timing signal: a16z is positioning defense/space/manufacturing as underappreciated by the broader market even as the category has become more fashionable — implies continued willingness to fund pre-consensus, unglamorous hard-tech founders rather than chase later, more visible rounds.
insights.quote: many of the companies that will matter most are being started right now, often in areas the rest of the market has been slow to take seriously
insights.locator: We believe American Dynamism is still early

themes.theme: How a16z evaluates and recruits investment talent

insights.claim: a16z's stated criterion for adding a General Partner in a specialized practice like American Dynamism is not primarily investment track record but depth of operator-level understanding of founders' businesses, evidenced by informal recurring engagement well before any deal.
insights.speaker: David Ulevitch
insights.so_what: Suggests a16z's competitive edge in defense/hard-tech deal sourcing is relationship depth built over months/years pre-deal rather than speed or valuation aggressiveness — a durable moat that's hard for newer funds entering the category to replicate quickly.
insights.quote: What convinced us wasn't the track record, strong as it is.
insights.locator: What convinced us wasn't the track record

insights.claim: Connor Love built his reputation among defense, space, and manufacturing founders by getting on calls with them every few weeks over long periods, independent of any live deal process, to track how their businesses and markets were actually evolving rather than how they appeared in pitch decks.
insights.speaker: David Ulevitch
insights.so_what: A concrete, replicable pattern for how top hard-tech investors source and win competitive deals: sustained non-transactional founder contact ahead of fundraises, not just reactive diligence once a round opens.
insights.quote: Long before a deal, Connor would get on calls with founders every few weeks to stay current, offer perspective, and build a real relationship
insights.locator: That kind of reputation is hard to earn

insights.claim: Connor Love is a West Point graduate and former active-duty U.S. Army Captain who, in 2019, chose to deploy to Northern Iraq alongside the joint military community and Kurdish partners instead of starting business school, before entering venture capital six years ago.
insights.speaker: David Ulevitch
insights.so_what: His operator background (leading soldiers, advising senior commanders in a real deployment) is being positioned as the credibility basis for evaluating defense-tech founders and DoD-adjacent business models — relevant when assessing how a16z's American Dynamism team sources judgment versus purely financial investors in the category.
insights.locator: Connor is a West Point graduate

insights.claim: a16z is appointing Connor Love as a General Partner in its American Dynamism practice, where he will back founders across defense, space, manufacturing, and autonomous systems.
insights.speaker: David Ulevitch
insights.so_what: A personnel move signaling continued/expanded a16z investment capacity specifically in defense, space, manufacturing, and autonomous systems — worth tracking which new deals in these sectors carry Connor Love's name going forward as a proxy for a16z's evolving thesis in the category.
insights.locator: I'm thrilled to welcome Connor Love
